blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (The Authorization header, with the bearer token, is logged at info level) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 is enough for a random 32-byte value; no bcrypt needed) in a `token_hash` column with a unique index, and look it up with `WHERE token_hash = $1` on the hash of the presented token — still an indexed equality, so the stated reason for storing it in clear does not hold. Anyone who reads the table today (a database backup, a replica, a read-only analyst account, an SQL injection elsewhere in the service) gets every user's live bearer credentials and can call the API as them, the same exposure the proposal's Why sets out to remove (CWE-312, CWE-256). Keep a short non-secret prefix if support needs to identify a token. Update task 1.1 and the spec ("shown once") accordingly.
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Redact `Authorization` (and `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, `Proxy-Authorization`) before logging; to let support see which token was sent, log the token's non-secret prefix or its id after lookup. As designed, anyone with access to the logs — support staff, the log aggregation service, a leaked log archive — copies a live token from any request line and replays it in `Authorization: Bearer` to act as that user (CWE-532). Task 1.3's test `logs_requests` should assert the header is redacted.
findings.title: The Authorization header, with the bearer token, is logged at info level

findings.recommendation: Ship at least a way to delete one's own token (or an expiry) with this change, or record the gap under Risks / Trade-offs with who decides it. The proposal's Why is that "a leaked integration exposes the account"; with this plan, once a token leaks (for instance through R-security-2's logs) the holder keeps full account access indefinitely and, unlike a password, the user has no way to change or cut it off. The Risks section only covers a lost token, not a leaked one.
findings.title: A leaked token cannot be revoked and never expires

findings.evidence: The service SHALL let a signed-in user create an API token, shown once, and SHALL accept it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header of later requests.
findings.location: specs/api-tokens/spec.md#Requirement: A user creates an API token
findings.recommendation: State whether "signed-in" includes a request authenticated by an API token. If it does, a stolen token can mint further tokens that survive any later revocation of the first one; require a password session (or a re-authentication) for the creation endpoint and add a scenario for it. Recorded with low confidence: the plan does not show the creation endpoint nor how the middleware marks a session as signed in.
findings.title: Authorization of token creation is not specified
